[[File:Mario_Ruben.jpg|thumb|245x245px|Mario Ruben in 2020]]

'''Mario Ruben''' (born 5 May 1968 in Rudolstadt, Germany) is a German chemist and university professor. Since 2013 he holds the research unit chair "Molecular Materials" and is director at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Klyatskaya|first=Svetlana (INT)|date=2018-11-29|title=INT- Molecular Materials|url=https://www.int.kit.edu/ruben.php|access-date=2020-08-13|website=www.int.kit.edu|language=en-gb}}</ref> and at the [[University of Strasbourg]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruben |first=Mario |title=Ruben (associé), Systèmes Quantiques Moléculaires  |url=https://isis.unistra.fr/cesq/equipes-associees/ruben-associe-systemes-quantiques-moleculaires/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |language=fr-fr}}</ref>

== Life ==

Mario Ruben studied chemistry from 1989 to 1994 at the Friedrich-Schiller-University Jena. In 1998, he obtained his PhD as fellow of the ''[[Studienstiftung|Studienstiftung des Deutschen Volkes]]'' with a work entitled ''Homo– and Heteronuclear Mg-Carbamato–Complexes for CO<sub>2</sub>–Activation'' at the [[University of Jena|Friedrich-Schiller-University Jena]] in the research group of Prof. Dr. Dirk Walther''.'' Afterwards, he completed a two-years research stay as [[German Academic Exchange Service|DAAD]]-fellow at the University of Strasbourg in the research group of Nobel laureate [[Jean-Marie Lehn]], where he habilitated in 2005 with a work on ''Functional'' (''Supra)Molecular Nanostructures.''<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ruben|first=Mario|date=2005-07-05|title=Functional (Supra)Molecular Nanostructures|url=http://www.ruben-group.de/lit/2005_20_habilitation_ruben.pdf|access-date=2020-08-13|website=|language=en}}</ref>

In 2012 he received a call to join the Faculty of Physics at the [[University of Münster]], Germany, which he declined to accept a W3 Full Professor position at the Faculty of Chemistry and Biology at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-04-06|title=Fakultät und Dekanat - Profs & PDs|url=https://www.chem-bio.kit.edu/113.php|access-date=2026-06-27|website=www.chem-bio.kit.edu|language=de-de}}</ref> In 2026, he received the 
[[European Research Council]] Advanced Grant.<ref>{{cite news |author=or|date=2026-06-23|title=ERC Advanced Grant für Mario Ruben vom KIT|url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/pi_2026_057_erc-advanced-grant-fuer-mario-ruben-vom-kit.php |trans-title=ERC Advanced Grant for Mario Ruben at KIT|work=Presseinformation KIT|language=de-de|location=Karlsruhe|publisher=KIT|access-date=2026-06-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=ERC Advanced Grants 2025: List of Principal Investigators – All domains|publisher=European Research Council|date=2026-06-23|url=https://erc.europa.eu/system/files/2026-06/erc-2025-adg-results-all-domains.pdf
|format=PDF|access-date=2026-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260624155239/https://erc.europa.eu/system/files/2026-06/erc-2025-adg-results-all-domains.pdf|archive-date=2026-06-24
}}</ref>

As of 2026, Ruben has 371 published works according to [[ORCID]]<ref>{{ORCID|0000-0002-7718-7016
}}</ref> and an [[h-index]] of 81 according to [[Google Scholar]].<ref>{{Google Scholar id}}</ref>

== Research topics ==

* CO<sub>2</sub>-activation and –transformation<ref>{{Cite news|last=Lossau|first=Norbert|date=2019-07-16|title=Kohlendioxid: Das Treibhausgas kann zu Graphen werden|language=de-de|work=DIE WELT|url=https://www.welt.de/wissenschaft/article196905811/Kohlendioxid-Das-Treibhausgas-kann-zu-Graphen-werden.html|access-date=2020-08-13}}</ref>
* Implementation of quantum algorithms in molecules
* Molecular battery materials
* Switchable magnetic compounds
* Optically detected nuclear magnetic resonance
